title: The Atlas
pitch: The report drawn as a map: regions become plates you open, places inside them hold the detail, and a locator inset says where you are.
bestFor: Research with distinct areas a reader explores in any order: landscape and market surveys, architecture overviews, multi-option comparisons, where 'where does this fit relative to everything else' matters.
weakness: The argument (findings → reconciliation → recommendation) is spread over pages, so a reader who wants one straight read follows links; the generated map shows relative weight, not real geography, and gets small on phones (numbered badges).
signals: parts differ in size or weight
a survey or landscape of options
avoid: a linear argument to read top to bottom
the answer depends mainly on time or dates
a dashboard of live numbers is the point
